Explain how a VPN works in simple words
11:55 PM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Your traffic goes into the tunnel locked up, comes out at a VPN company's computer, and only then reaches the website.

Here is what that means in practice:

Locked up: Your Wi-Fi owner or internet provider can see you are connected to a VPN, but not which sites you visit or what you send.
New address: Websites see the VPN's address instead of yours, so your location looks different.
Trust moves: The VPN company can now see what your provider used to see. So pick one you trust.

It helps on public Wi-Fi and for privacy from your provider. It does not make you anonymous, and it won't stop viruses or scams.
